LESSON: ORAL PRESENTATIONS

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 10.1.1: Oral Presentations

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Oral Presentations. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How can one improve the presentation of a song to make it interesting?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify features of songs in the locality
2. use performance techniques when singing
3. write songs on a scientific innovation
4. appreciate the role of songs in the society

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: ORAL PRESENTATIONS
Subject: ENGLISH · Grade: Grade 8
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Oral Presentations helps you succeed in ENGLISH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: ORAL PRESENTATIONS
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify features of songs in the locality

What this means
In this part you learn to identify features of songs in the locality. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify features of songs in the locality.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Oral Presentations”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify features of songs in the locality. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Use performance techniques when singing

What this means
In this part you learn to use performance techniques when singing. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use performance techniques when singing.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Oral Presentations to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use performance techniques when singing. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Write songs on a scientific innovation

What this means
In this part you learn to write songs on a scientific innovation. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: write songs on a scientific innovation.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can write songs on a scientific innovation. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Appreciate the role of songs in the society

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the role of songs in the society. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the role of songs in the society.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Oral Presentations”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the role of songs in the society. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Oral Presentations is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Oral Presentations”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify features of songs in the locality)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Oral Presentations to a partner. (skill: use performance techniques when singing)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: write songs on a scientific innovation)

Example 4: Read a short paragraph about “Oral Presentations”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: appreciate the role of songs in the society)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Oral Presentations to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify features of songs in the locality.
3. Practise this skill: use performance techniques when singing.
4. Practise this skill: write songs on a scientific innovation.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Oral Presentations from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Oral Presentations: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 8 learner study Oral Presentations?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can one improve the presentation of a song to make it interesting?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Oral Presentations means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify features of songs in the locality.
5. Be able to: use performance techniques when singing.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
